mysh

march 2026 · CSC209, University of Toronto

A Unix-like shell in C, built to understand what happens between entering a command and seeing its output.

I developed MYSH for Software Tools and Systems Programming. It brought together process creation, inter-process communication, memory management, and low-level Unix programming.

what it does

  • Parses commands and executes built-in and external programs.
  • Manages dynamically allocated environment variables with custom expansion.
  • Coordinates processes through fork, exec, and wait.
  • Connects commands through pipelines and handles signals and background jobs.
  • Provides filesystem utilities with recursive traversal and error handling.
  • Supports socket-based client-server messaging across concurrent processes.

under the hood

External commands run in child processes while the shell retains control of the session. Pipelines connect those processes through file descriptors, with pipe and dup2 redirecting standard input and output.

Signal handling separates the shell's lifecycle from the commands it launches. Foreground commands can be interrupted while background work is tracked and completed processes are reaped.

the details that mattered

Command parsing requires careful ownership of dynamically allocated strings. Consistent cleanup routines and Valgrind checks helped catch leaks. GDB provided a way to inspect the state behind failed system calls and process-management bugs.

File descriptors needed just as much attention: unused pipe ends must be closed in both parent and child processes, otherwise a program can wait indefinitely for input or exhaust its resources. Background processes also need to be reaped without blocking the interactive shell.

built with

C, Unix system calls, sockets, Make, Valgrind, GDB, and Git.

Possible future extensions include command history, tab completion, scripting, expanded job-control commands, and wildcard expansion.

source availability

The code is private under university academic-integrity policies. Contact me to discuss the implementation or request a review.
